result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Answer B caps the text at about 70ch and centres it using padding with max(). It also adds a 1rem minimum gap on phones, changes only the two affected rules, and keeps the header background full width. One check in B is wrong: at 1000px the 70ch cap (roughly 600–650px in Georgia at 17px) is narrower than the screen, not wider, though the CSS itself still works. Answer A's 960px max-width allows lines well over 100 characters and it reprints the whole stylesheet, but it does explain the header-background choice more clearly. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Answer A meets the main request better: its max() padding caps text at about 70ch, centers it, and keeps a 1rem minimum on phones, and it shows only the two changed rules. Answer B's 960px max-width is about 110+ characters at 17px Georgia, which is too wide to read comfortably, and it repeats the whole stylesheet instead of showing only the changes. B does explicitly say the green header background stays full width and adds a useful viewport meta tip, but A's approach also keeps the background full width, though it doesn't say so outright.
